nodes.name: Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement:
Fix some $1 < \alpha \leq 2$ and consider an $\alpha$-HSBT $\mathcal{T}$
realized by a full binary tree of height $h$.
Let $R$ be a request set over $\mathcal{T}$ and let ${\mathcal{A}}^{*}$ be
some benchmark offline MPMD algorithm for $\mathcal{T}$, $R$.
The stilt-walker algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ guarantees that
\[
\mathbb{E} \left[ \mathrm{cost}_{\mathcal{A}} \left( R, \mathcal{T} \right) \right]
\leq
O (1 / (\alpha - 1)) \cdot \mathrm{cost}^{\mathit{s}}_{{\mathcal{A}}^{*}} \left( R,
\mathcal{T} \right)
+
O (h) \cdot \mathrm{cost}^{\mathit{t}}_{{\mathcal{A}}^{*}} \left( R, \mathcal{T} \right)
+
\beta  \, ,
\]
where
$\beta = \beta(\mathcal{T})$
depends only on $\mathcal{T}$ and is independent of $R$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement:
There exists some
$\zeta = \zeta(R)$
such that the time potentials satisfy
\[
\mathrm{cost}^{\mathit{t}}_{\mathcal{A}}(R, \mathcal{T})
\leq
\zeta + \sum_{v \in T - \mathcal{L}} O (\tau_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}}))
\quad \text{and} \quad
\mathrm{cost}^{\mathit{t}}_{{\mathcal{A}}^{*}}(R, \mathcal{T})
\geq
\zeta / h + \sum_{v \in T - \mathcal{L}} \Omega ({\tau}^{*}_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}}) / h)
\]
(recall that $h$ denotes the height of $T$).
The space potentials satisfy
\[
\mathrm{cost}^{\mathit{s}}_{\mathcal{A}}(R, \mathcal{T})
\leq
\mathit{c}_{\mathrm{end}}^{\mathit{s}} + \sum_{v \in T - \mathcal{L}} O (\sigma_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}}))
\quad \text{and} \quad
\mathrm{cost}^{\mathit{s}}_{{\mathcal{A}}^{*}}(R, \mathcal{T})
\geq
\sum_{v \in T - \mathcal{L}} \Omega ((\alpha - 1) \cdot {\sigma}^{*}_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}}))
\]
(recall that the parameter $\alpha$ is set in Thm.{}~4.1).

nodes.name: Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement:
For every $v \in T - \mathcal{L}$, it holds that
$\mathbb{E}[\tau_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}})]
\leq
O ({\tau}^{*}_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}}) + {\sigma}^{*}_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}}) + w(v))$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement:
For every $v \in T - \mathcal{L}$, it holds that
$\mathbb{E}[\sigma_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}})]
\leq
\mathbb{E}[\tau_{v}(0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}})]$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.7
nodes.statement:
For every phase
$\phi = [t_{0}, t_{1})$
of $v$, it holds that
$\mathbb{E}_{v}[\sigma(\phi)]
=
\mathbb{E}_{v}[\tau(\phi)]$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.10
nodes.statement:
The partition of $[0, \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{end}})$ into phases satisfies the following three
properties: \\
(P1)
if
$t < \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{late}}$,
then
$\mathbb{E}_{\mathit{anc}(v)} \left[ \int_{T^{-}}^{T^{+}} X(s) d s \mid T^{-} = t
\right]
\geq
w(v) (1 - 1 / e)$; \\
(P2)
$|P_{\mathrm{early}}| \leq K + 1$; and \\
(P3)
$\mathbb{E}_{\mathit{anc}(v)}[|P_{\mathrm{late}}|] = O (1)$
with an exponentially vanishing upper tail.

nodes.name: Corollary 4.1
nodes.statement:
If
$\phi$ is a $0$-phase that starts at time
$T^{-} = t < \mathit{t}_{\mathrm{late}}$,
then
$\mathbb{E}_{\mathit{anc}(v)}[{\tau}^{*}(\phi) + {\sigma}^{*}(\phi) \mid T^{-} = t]
\geq
\Omega (w(v))$.
